question: Krishna River flows through ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Krishna River rises at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra (Western Ghats) and flows eastwards through Karnataka and Telangana before entering Andhra Pradesh, where it drains into the Bay of Bengal. (कृष्णा नदी — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Krishna is the second longest river of peninsular India (about 1,400 km) after the Godavari.

• Its major tributaries are the Bhima, Tungabhadra, Koyna, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha and Musi.

• Important dams on the Krishna basin: Almatti and Narayanpur (Karnataka), Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana).

NOTE

• The Krishna does not flow through Tamil Nadu, Odisha or Kerala. Peninsular east-flowing rivers: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri — all draining into the Bay of Bengal.

question: Who among the following sang the famous Bollywood song "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arijit Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Bollywood title track "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil" (from the 2016 film of the same name) was sung by Arijit Singh. The music was composed by Pritam and the lyrics were written by Amitabh Bhattacharya. (अरिजीत सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Arijit Singh rose to fame with "Tum Hi Ho" (Aashiqui 2) and has won the National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer and several Filmfare Awards.

• The film "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil" was directed by Karan Johar.

NOTE

• Neeti Mohan and Shreya Ghoshal are leading female playback singers; Sukhbir is known chiefly for Punjabi pop songs such as "Ishq Tera Tadpave".

question: In which of the following Articles is "Protection against arrest and detention" mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 22.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 22 of the Indian Constitution provides "Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases". It guarantees an arrested person the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest, the right to consult a lawyer of his choice, and the right to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest (excluding travel time). (अनुच्छेद 22 — गिरफ्तारी और निरोध से संरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 20 — Protection in respect of conviction for offences (no ex-post-facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination).

• Article 21 — Protection of life and personal liberty; Article 21A — Right to Education.

• Article 24 — Prohibition of employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines and hazardous work.

• Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

NOTE

• Articles 19–22 together form the Right to Freedom. Article 22 also lays down safeguards regarding preventive detention (normally not beyond 3 months without an Advisory Board's opinion).

question: The Airavatesvara Temple in Tamil Nadu was built by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajaraja Chola II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram (Kumbakonam), Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola king Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century CE. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva. (ऐरावतेश्वर मंदिर — राजराज चोल द्वितीय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of the "Great Living Chola Temples", a UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur (built by Rajaraja Chola I) and the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram (built by Rajendra Chola I).

• The temple takes its name from Airavata, the white elephant of Indra, who is said to have worshipped Shiva here.

NOTE

• The Chola temples are the finest examples of Dravidian architecture, with a towering vimana, a pillared mandapa and elaborate stone sculptures.

question: Which of the following is the first month in the Islamic lunar calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muharram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Muharram" is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) lunar calendar. It is one of the four sacred months in Islam, and its 10th day (Ashura) is observed in remembrance of the martyrdom of Imam Hussain at the Battle of Karbala. (मुहर्रम — इस्लामी कैलेंडर का पहला महीना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The twelve months of the Hijri calendar in order: Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Thani, Jumada al-Awwal, Jumada al-Thani, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah.

• Ramzan (Ramadan) is the 9th month, the month of fasting; Shawwal is the 10th month, and Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated on its first day.

NOTE

• The Islamic calendar is purely lunar with 354/355 days, so its months shift about 10–11 days earlier each year relative to the Gregorian calendar. It began with the Hijra (migration of Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina) in 622 CE.

question: The materials, through which things cannot be seen, are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is opaque materials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Opaque materials" are those through which light cannot pass at all, so objects on the other side cannot be seen. Examples: wood, stone, metal, cardboard, a brick wall. (अपारदर्शी पदार्थ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Transparent materials allow light to pass through completely, so objects are seen clearly — e.g., clear glass, water, air.

• Translucent materials allow light to pass partially, so objects are seen hazily/blurred — e.g., butter paper, frosted glass, oiled paper.

• "Pale" simply means light in colour and is not an optical classification.

NOTE

• Opaque objects form sharp shadows because they block light completely. The formation of shadows and eclipses depends on light travelling in straight lines (rectilinear propagation).

question: There were several cities in the Maurya empire. Which of the following cities was located on the southernmost side?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmagiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given Mauryan centres, "Brahmagiri" (in present-day Chitradurga district, Karnataka) lay the furthest south. It is famous for a set of Ashokan minor rock edicts and marks the southern reach of the Mauryan empire. (ब्रह्मगिरि — सबसे दक्षिणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Girnar (Junagadh, Gujarat) — site of Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts and later the Rudradaman inscription on the Sudarshana Lake.

• Topra (Haryana) — the original site of the pillar later moved to Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq (Delhi-Topra pillar).

• Rupnath (Madhya Pradesh) — site of an Ashokan minor rock edict.

NOTE

• Mauryan provincial capitals: Pataliputra (imperial capital), Taxila (north-west), Ujjain (west), Tosali (east/Kalinga) and Suvarnagiri (south). The empire's southern limit stopped short of the Tamil kingdoms (Cholas, Cheras, Pandyas).

question: Kitab ul-Hind, an Arabic text was written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Al- Biruni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kitab-ul-Hind" (also called Tahqiq-i-Hind) is an Arabic work written by Al-Biruni, the Central Asian scholar who came to India in the 11th century along with Mahmud of Ghazni. It describes Indian religion, philosophy, sciences, customs, astronomy and the caste system. (किताब-उल-हिंद — अलबरूनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan traveller who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, wrote "Rihla" (in Arabic).

• Ziauddin Barani wrote "Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi" and "Fatwa-i-Jahandari" (in Persian).

• Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni was the invader who raided India seventeen times, most famously sacking the Somnath temple (1025 CE).

NOTE

• Al-Biruni is often called the "Father of Indology". He learnt Sanskrit and studied the Vedas, the Puranas, the Bhagavad Gita and works of Indian mathematics and astronomy.

question: The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill-2022 is related to which ______ of the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of External Affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022" was introduced in Parliament by the Ministry of External Affairs. It amends the parent Act of 2005 to additionally prohibit the financing of any activity related to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems. (विदेश मंत्रालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) include biological, chemical and nuclear weapons.

• The amendment empowers the Central Government to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets of persons suspected of such financing.

• It brings India's law in line with the requirements of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and UN Security Council Resolution 1540.

NOTE

• India follows a "No First Use" (NFU) nuclear doctrine and maintains a policy of credible minimum deterrence. India is a member of the MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement and Australia Group, though not of the NSG.

question: Gulabo Sapera is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera is the renowned exponent who popularised the "Kalbelia" folk dance of Rajasthan on the world stage. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — गुलाबो सपेरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kalbelia is performed by the women of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan; the swirling black skirts and serpentine movements imitate a snake's motion.

• It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Instruments used include the been (pungi), khanjari, dholak and morchang.

NOTE

• Other Rajasthani folk dances: Ghoomar, Bhavai, Chari, Terah Taali and Kachhi Ghodi. Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Odissi (Odisha) and Kathakali (Kerala) are classical, not folk, forms.

question: Which of the following acids makes the pH of vinegar acidic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetic acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinegar is a dilute (about 5–8%) aqueous solution of "acetic acid (CH₃COOH)", which is what makes its pH acidic (roughly 2.4–3.4). Acetic acid is a weak carboxylic acid with the common name ethanoic acid. (सिरका — ऐसीटिक अम्ल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Tartaric acid — found in tamarind and grapes; used in baking powder.

• Citric acid — found in lemon, orange and other citrus fruits.

• Linoleic acid — an essential fatty acid found in vegetable oils, not a food acidulant.

NOTE

• Natural acids: lactic acid (curd/milk), oxalic acid (tomato, spinach), malic acid (apple), formic acid (ant sting), butyric acid (rancid butter), ascorbic acid (Vitamin C, amla). Glacial acetic acid is pure (nearly 100%) acetic acid, which freezes below 16.6°C.

question: How many bronze medals did India win in the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in the year 2021)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in July–August 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic), India won a total of 7 medals — 1 gold, 2 silver and 4 bronze, its best-ever Olympic haul. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020 — 4 कांस्य पदक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Gold (1): Neeraj Chopra — Javelin throw (India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics).

• Silver (2): Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting, 49 kg) and Ravi Kumar Dahiya (wrestling, 57 kg).

• Bronze (4): P. V. Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing, 69 kg), Bajrang Punia (wrestling, 65 kg) and the Indian Men's Hockey Team (its first Olympic medal in 41 years).

NOTE

• P. V. Sindhu became the first Indian woman to win two individual Olympic medals (silver at Rio 2016, bronze at Tokyo 2020). India finished 48th on the Tokyo medal tally.

question: Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks are included in which measure of money supply?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the RBI's classification of money supply, "M2" = M1 + savings deposits with Post Office savings banks. Hence Post Office savings deposits first appear in M2. (एम2 — डाकघर बचत जमा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• M1 (narrow money) = Currency with the public + Demand deposits with the banking system + "Other" deposits with the RBI.

• M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks.

• M3 (broad money) = M1 + Time deposits with the banking system — this is the most widely used aggregate monetary resource.

• M4 = M3 + All deposits with Post Office savings banks (excluding National Savings Certificates).

NOTE

• Liquidity order: M1 > M2 > M3 > M4 (M1 is the most liquid, M4 the least). M1 and M2 are called narrow money, while M3 and M4 are called broad money.

question: According to the 2011 census, what is the approximate female literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, the female literacy rate was about 65.46% (approximately 65%), while the male literacy rate was about 82.14% and the overall literacy rate was 74.04%. (2011 जनगणना — महिला साक्षरता लगभग 65%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest literacy rate (94%) and Bihar the lowest (61.8%) in Census 2011.

• Sex ratio (2011) — 943 females per 1000 males; Kerala highest (1084), Haryana lowest (879).

• A person aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is counted as literate.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence. The first synchronous census in India was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding fertilizers?
option_2: They are very rich in plant nutrients
option_3: They provide humus to the soil
solution_text:
The correct answer is They provide humus to the soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fertilizers do NOT provide humus to the soil — this statement is incorrect. Humus is supplied by manure (organic matter such as decomposed plant and animal waste), not by chemical fertilizers. (उर्वरक मिट्टी को ह्यूमस नहीं देते)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other statements are correct: fertilizers are prepared in factories, are man-made inorganic salts, and are rich in specific plant nutrients (N, P, K).

• Examples of fertilizers: urea, ammonium sulphate, superphosphate, NPK, potash.

NOTE

• Manure vs Fertilizer — Manure: natural/organic, adds humus, improves soil texture and water-holding capacity, nutrient-poor per unit. Fertilizer: chemical/inorganic, nutrient-rich, gives quick results, but excessive use causes soil degradation and water eutrophication.

question: What is the term of State legislative assembly in India as per Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The normal term of a State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is five years from the date of its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier by the Governor. (विधान सभा का कार्यकाल — 5 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• During a National Emergency (Article 352), the term may be extended by Parliament by one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.

• The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent house that is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, and each member has a term of six years.

• The Lok Sabha also has a normal term of 5 years; the Rajya Sabha is permanent.

NOTE

• Minimum age: 25 years for the Legislative Assembly and 30 years for the Legislative Council. The maximum strength of an Assembly is 500 and the minimum is 60 (with special exceptions such as Sikkim, Goa and Mizoram).

question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact signed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1931.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gandhi-Irwin Pact" was signed on 5 March 1931 in Delhi between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy of India. Under it, Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference in London. (गांधी-इरविन समझौता — 1931)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In return, the Government agreed to release political prisoners (not those guilty of violence), withdraw ordinances, return confiscated property and allow the peaceful picketing of liquor and foreign-cloth shops and the making of salt for personal use in coastal areas.

• It is also known as the Delhi Pact. Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931) as the sole representative of the Congress.

NOTE

• Timeline: Simon Commission — 1928; Lahore Session/Purna Swaraj — 1929; Dandi March/Civil Disobedience — 1930; Gandhi-Irwin Pact — 1931; Poona Pact — 1932; Government of India Act — 1935.

question: The weather pattern of a place, made on the basis of the aggregate weather data collected over a long period, such as 25 years, is called the ______ of that place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Climate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Climate" is the sum total (average) of the weather conditions of a place over a long period, generally taken as 25 to 30 years or more. It describes the general pattern, whereas weather describes the atmospheric condition at a particular time and place. (जलवायु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Elements of weather and climate: temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation.

• Factors controlling climate: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, relief and prevailing winds.

• India has a tropical monsoon climate, dominated by the seasonal reversal of winds.

NOTE

• "Ecology" is the study of the relationship between organisms and their surroundings; "landforms" are the physical features of the Earth's surface; "environment" is the total surroundings (biotic + abiotic) of an organism.

question: Which of the following books was NOT written by Aravind Adiga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Cost of Living.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Cost of Living" was NOT written by Aravind Adiga — it is a collection of essays by Arundhati Roy (1999), dealing with big dams and India's development policy. (द कॉस्ट ऑफ लिविंग — अरुंधति रॉय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Books written by Aravind Adiga: "The White Tiger" (winner of the Man Booker Prize, 2008), "Between the Assassinations", "Last Man in Tower", "Selection Day" and "Amnesty".

• The White Tiger was adapted into a Netflix film in 2021.

NOTE

• Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997 for "The God of Small Things"; her other works include "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" and "Walking with the Comrades". Other Indian-origin Booker winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Kiran Desai (2006).

question: The British Parliament passed the Regulating Act in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1773.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1773. It was the first step by the British Government to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट — 1773)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Key provisions of the Regulating Act, 1773:

◦ It designated the Governor of Bengal as the "Governor-General of Bengal" — Warren Hastings became the first — and created an Executive Council of four members.

◦ It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal.

◦ It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) with one Chief Justice and three other judges.

◦ It prohibited Company servants from engaging in private trade and accepting bribes or gifts from Indians.

NOTE

• Later constitutional landmarks: Pitt's India Act (1784), Charter Act of 1813/1833/1853, Government of India Act 1858 (Crown rule), Indian Councils Acts 1861/1892/1909, Government of India Acts 1919 and 1935.

question: On 8 September 2022, NITI Aayog, in collaboration with ______, launched the country's first national electric freight platform - Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport - India (e-FAST India).
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Resources Institute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 8 September 2022, NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the "World Resources Institute (WRI) India", launched India's first national electric freight platform — e-FAST India (Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport - India). (विश्व संसाधन संस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• e-FAST India aims to accelerate the electrification of freight/trucking in India by building awareness, supporting pilot projects and enabling policy dialogue among stakeholders.

• The platform was supported by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, among others.

• Freight transport contributes a large share of transport-sector CO₂ emissions in India, so electrifying trucks is central to the net-zero-by-2070 goal.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister, and it has a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO.

question: By the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022, the period given to the Central Government for removing any difficulty arising in giving effect to the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019 has been extended to ______ years from the date of commencement of the Act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (Amendment) Bill, 2022" extended the time available to the Central Government to issue orders removing difficulties in giving effect to the parent Act from two years to five years from the date of commencement of the Act. (5 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The New Delhi International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019 set up the NDIAC as an institution of national importance to promote institutional arbitration in India.

• The 2022 amendment also renamed the centre as the "India International Arbitration Centre".

• "Removal of difficulties" clauses are a standard feature of Indian statutes, allowing the Government to issue clarifying orders within a limited window.

NOTE

• Arbitration in India is chiefly governed by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (amended in 2015, 2019 and 2021), which is based on the UNCITRAL Model Law.

question: Kajari is a folk song and dance style of India. It originated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kajari (Kajri)" is a semi-classical folk song and dance form that originated in Uttar Pradesh, particularly in the Mirzapur, Varanasi and Bhojpuri-speaking region. It is sung during the monsoon month of Sawan (Bhadon) and expresses the longing of a wife for her husband who is away. (कजरी — उत्तर प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kajari is closely associated with the Kajari Teej festival and is traditionally sung by women in groups during the rainy season.

• Other folk traditions of Uttar Pradesh: Birha, Chaiti, Sohar, Rasiya, Charkula, Nautanki, Raslila and Khyal.

NOTE

• Regional folk forms: Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Baul/Chhau (West Bengal), Ottamthullal/Theyyam (Kerala), Lavani (Maharashtra), Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat).

question: In cricket, hitting the ball in the air in such a way that it goes beyond the boundary is equal to ______ runs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In cricket, if the batter strikes the ball so that it clears the boundary without touching the ground inside the field, the batting side is awarded six (6) runs. (छक्का — 6 रन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• If the ball touches the ground before crossing (or rolls over) the boundary, four (4) runs are awarded.

• Cricket's laws are framed by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), and the sport is governed internationally by the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered in Dubai, UAE.

• The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) was established in 1928.

NOTE

• Cricket terms: over (6 legal balls), maiden over (no runs conceded), hat-trick (three wickets in three consecutive balls), duck (dismissed for zero), century (100 runs), LBW (leg before wicket). Yuvraj Singh famously hit six sixes in an over against England in the 2007 T20 World Cup.

question: According to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, India is a ______ country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Republic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India to be a "SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC". A "Republic" means the head of the State (the President) is elected and not a hereditary monarch, and every public office is open to every citizen without discrimination. (गणराज्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The words "SOCIALIST", "SECULAR" and "INTEGRITY" were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

• The Preamble secures to all citizens Justice (social, economic and political), Liberty (of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship), Equality (of status and opportunity) and promotes Fraternity (assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation).

• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

NOTE

• The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and can be amended without damaging its basic structure. Being secular, India is not a "religious" state — so Option 1 is wrong.
